key_insight: Rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent design of printable scaffold microstructures and their spatial placement to meet whole-bone mechanical targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports highly porous bone scaffolds that preserve target mechanical responses while enforcing feature-size constraints.
method: Generate periodic lattice cells with a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize cell geometry and spatial assignment under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: Computational benchmarks report under 1% error across six prescribed moduli for all eight rabbit-case refinements, plus human femoral scaffolds with 63% and 84% porosity meeting reported compliance or strain-energy targets.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational validation; physical printability, fatigue performance, and biological integration remain to be demonstrated experimentally.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
